name: Porata
title: Son of Haman
summary: Porata was one of the ten sons of Haman, the Agagite, who was an enemy of the Jewish people in the Persian Empire. He was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves against their enemies according to King Ahasuerus's decree. His death marked God's protection of His people and is celebrated during the festival of Purim.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Plan Against the Jews
keyEvents.description: Porata's father Haman planned to destroy all the Jews in the Persian Empire after a conflict with Mordecai.

keyEvents.title: Esther's Intercession
keyEvents.description: Queen Esther pleaded for her people before King Ahasuerus and exposed Haman's evil plan.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Execution
keyEvents.description: Haman, Porata's father, was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.

keyEvents.title: The Jews' Victory and Porata's Death
keyEvents.description: Porata was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves against their enemies on the 13th day of the month of Adar.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Ten Sons Hanged
keyEvents.description: At Esther's request, the bodies of Haman's ten sons, including Porata, were hung up for public display in Susa.
